title: Commonwealth LNG Expansion, LLC submits request to initiate Pre-Filing Review for the Commonwealth LNG Expansion Project under PF26-18.

documents.name: 2026-09-23 CWLNG Expansion Pre-File Request - Public.pdf
documents.text:
September 23, 2026


Debbie-Anne A. Reese
Secretary
Federal Energy Regulatory Commission
888 First Street, NE
Washington, D.C. 20426

Re:    Commonwealth LNG Expansion, LLC
       Request to Initiate NEPA Pre-Filing Process
       Commonwealth LNG Expansion Project
       Cameron Parish, Louisiana
       Docket No. PF26- - 000


Dear Ms. Reese:

Pursuant to Section 157.21 of the Commission’s regulations, Commonwealth LNG Expansion,
LLC (“CWLNG Expansion Co”) hereby requests that the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission
(“Commission” or “FERC”) initiate the Commission’s National Environmental Policy Act
(“NEPA”) pre-filing review of CWLNG Expansion Co’s proposed expansion project to be located
in Cameron Parish, Louisiana (“Expansion Project” or “Project”). The Expansion Project is
proposed to be located adjacent to the authorized Commonwealth LNG Project under FERC
Docket No. CP19-502 (“Base Project”) and is being developed to liquefy domestic natural gas for
export to foreign markets as liquefied natural gas (“LNG”). The Project is proposed to be sited,
constructed and operated pursuant to Section 3 of the Natural Gas Act (“NGA”).

In compliance with the Commission’s mandatory pre-filing procedures, CWLNG Expansion Co
submits the following information:

1.     Project Schedule (18 C.F.R. § 157.21(d)(1))

CWLNG Expansion Co anticipates filing its formal application in April 2027 and will respectfully
request that the Commission issue an Order authorizing the siting, construction and operation of
the Project no later than July 2028. A more detailed requested schedule is provided below.




                  730 Town and Country Blvd. • Suite 350 • Houston, Texas • 77024
                         Telephone: (346) 352-4444 • Fax: (346) 352-8909
                                     Proposed Expansion Project Schedule

     Commonwealth submits Pre-Filing Request                              September 23, 2026

     OEP Director issues letter commencing Pre-Filing Process               October 1, 2026

     Commonwealth conducts an Open House                                    November 2026

     Commonwealth files Application                                            April 2027

     FERC issues Final Environmental Impact Statement                          May 2028

     FERC issues Order Granting Section 3 Authorization                        July 2028

     FERC issues Notice to Proceed with Construction                        September 2028

     First LNG                                                              December 2032

     Expansion Project In-Service                                              May 2033

2.        Zoning (18 C.F.R. § 157.21(d)(2))

The Expansion Project will be located on an approximately 200-acre parcel of land in Cameron
Parish, Louisiana, on the west side of the Calcasieu Ship Channel, near its entrance into the Gulf of
America (the “Project Site”). The Project Site has no zoning classification regulation or land use
restrictions and is suitable for use by the proposed Project. The parcels of property that comprise
the Project Site are either owned or under the control of Commonwealth Expansion Co. Location
maps and a site plan are attached as Appendix A.

3.        Project Description (18 C.F.R. § 157.21(d)(4))

CWLNG Expansion Co proposes to construct five additional natural gas liquefaction trains and
appurtenant facilities and one additional LNG storage tank with a nominal capacity of 220,000
cubic meters (“m3”). Each liquefaction train will be driven directly by a combustion turbine, and
onsite power will be provided by four smaller combustion turbines. Additional feed gas will be
provided by a 42-inch-diameter intrastate (non-jurisdictional) natural gas pipeline lateral, from the
Gillis Hub, approximately 63-miles in length, permitted and constructed separately. The
Expansion Project will utilize the Base Project’s marine loading berth (capable of loading LNG
carriers (“LNGC”) up to a capacity of 216,000 m3), dredged slip, and turning basin. A new marine
offloading facility (“MOF”) and heavy-haul road will facilitate delivery of materials, including
piperack, pretreatment, and liquefaction modules. The Project will include shoreline protection to
prevent coastal erosion. The Expansion Project will roughly double the Base Project’s total
nominal liquefaction and production capacity to approximately 18.0 million metric tonnes per
annum (“MTPA”) of LNG, which will be exported by LNGCs and delivered to global markets,
beginning in late-2032.
 A more detailed description of the FERC-jurisdictional facilities for the Project is as follows:

Feed Gas Pretreatment: The Project will include five (5) pretreatment modules (one (1) per
liquefaction train); each with a mercury guard bed, acid gas removal, and dehydration.

Liquefaction: Following pretreatment, feed gas will continue to the liquefaction trains, which will
use the Honeywell Single Mixed Refrigerant (“SMR”) process. The feed gas will be condensed in
the liquefaction unit as it is contacted with progressively cooler mixed refrigerants until it is fully
condensed. The SMR process uses only one MR loop for precooling, liquefaction, and subcooling,
providing the benefit of reduced equipment count.

LNG Storage: The Project will include one (1) 220,000 m3 (net capacity) full-containment LNG
storage tank.

Boil-Off Gas: Vapor-stage natural gas (e.g., from “heat leaks”) will feed into the Boil-Off Gas
(“BOG”) compressors, which incorporate multiple stage compression and inter-cooling. The gas
will be compressed in the BOG compressors and returned to the liquefaction process upstream of
the feed gas booster compressors or utilized as supplemental fuel gas for the Project.

Power Supply: Power for the operation of the Project is expected to be generated by a direct drive,
simple cycle gas turbine power plant. Emergency power will be provided by a diesel generator
with black start capability and security systems will include battery back-up.

Storm Protection: The Project will be protected from potential storm surge by a perimeter surge
wall.

Control, Hazard Detection, and Mitigation Systems: The Project Control Room will contain state-
of-the-art control and hazard detection systems. These systems will provide local and remote
monitoring and control, fire protection, and emergency shutdown capability

Flare System: The flare system will be designed to handle plant upset relief loads and will include
a flare stack and knockout drums, which will be sited in accordance with applicable safety
requirements, away from LNG storage tanks and processing areas.

Marine Offloading Facility: The MOF will accommodate delivery of piperack, pretreatment, and
liquefaction modules for transport on the proposed heavy-haul road. The MOF, which will remain
in place following construction, will include a pile-supported platform, sheetpile bulkhead, and
dredged approach channel from the existing Calcasieu Ship Channel. The Expansion Project will
use the Base Project’s marine loading facilities without modification.

4.     Relevant Federal and State Agencies (18 C.F.R. § 157.21(d)(5))

Appendix B includes a table identifying the federal, state, and local agencies that have jurisdiction
over the Expansion Project. These agencies received notification on September 22, 2026, of
CWLNG Expansion Co’s intent to engage in the pre-filing process. CWLNG Expansion Co
intends to pursue such approvals during pre-filing and anticipates relevant agencies will issue their
 respective permits concurrently with the FERC review process. Accordingly, Commonwealth
Expansion Co has accounted for agency schedules for issuance of federal authorizations.

5.     Other Persons/Organizations Contacted about the Project (18 C.F.R. § 157.21(d)(6))

CWLNG Expansion Co has begun discussions with various stakeholders regarding the proposed
Project. As further described in Section 9 below, CWLNG Expansion Co will continue to meet
with various groups and individuals and will continue work to ensure all relevant stakeholders
have been identified and provided an opportunity to participate in the development process.
Appendix C provides tables which detail stakeholder and interested party contacts identified to
date.

6.     Project Work Already Completed (18 C.F.R. § 157.21(d)(7))

To date, CWLNG Expansion Co has already initiated stakeholder and agency engagement and
various planning and development work for the Project, which include the following:
       • Engagement of the following consultants;
                TRC Environmental Corporation – FERC Application & Permitting Support;
                C-K and Associates – Air Permitting and Modeling;
                T. Baker Smith – U.S. Army Corps of Engineers Permitting and Coastal
                  Management Permitting;
                AcuTech – Waterway Suitability Assessment (“WSA”) and U.S. Coast Guard;
                Moffit and Nickol – Marine Berthing Analysis; and
                Technip – Engineering, Procurement, and Construction.
       • Acquisition of property for the proposed Project Site;
       • Phase I Environmental Site Assessments;
       • Wetland Delineations & Protected-Species Habitat Surveys;
       • Meetings with various regulatory agencies and stakeholders;
       • Consultations with the U.S. Coast Guard for the Preliminary WSA; and
       • Developed Project website.

7.     Third Party Consultant Proposals (18 C.F.R. § 157.21(d)(8))

CWLNG Expansion Co widely distributed a request for proposals to potential third-party
contractors on September 3, 2026, and received six responses. CWLNG Expansion Co is providing
the response packages from all responding firms to the Commission Staff, for review and selection,
as specified in the February 2025 revision of the Handbook for Using Third-Party Contractors to
Prepare Environmental Documents for Natural Gas Facilities and Hydropower Projects. CWLNG
Expansion Co has reviewed the proposals for the Organizational Conflict of Interest (“OCI”) and
certified each proposal, accordingly, provided in Appendix D. Appendix D is being filed as
Privileged and Confidential information pursuant to Section 388.112 of the Commission’s
regulations.

CWLNG Expansion Co understands that upon issuance of the Commission’s approval of the
request to use the pre-filing process, a signed Memorandum of Understanding between
Commission staff, CWLNG Expansion Co, and the selected third-party contractor will be posted
 to the public docket. In accordance with 18 C.F.R. § 157.21(f)(2), CWLNG Expansion Co will
execute a contract with the selected third-party contractor and notify Commission staff within 14
days of issuance of the Commission’s acceptance into pre-filing letter.

8.     Acknowledgement of Complete Environmental Report and Complete Application
       Required at the Time of Filing (18 C.F.R. § 157.21(d)(10))

CWLNG Expansion Co acknowledges that a complete Environmental Report and a complete
application under Section 3 of the NGA must be submitted to the Commission at the time of filing.

9.     Public Participation Plan (18 C.F.R. § 157.21(d)(11))

During the pre-filing process, CWLNG Expansion Co will work to identify and resolve all
potential issues and concerns of stakeholders, thereby providing the Commission with a robust and
complete application.

CWLNG Expansion Co has developed a Public Participation Plan to facilitate stakeholder
communications, public information sharing and ongoing engagement regarding the Expansion
Project. The plan is designed to provide timely, accurate and transparent information to
stakeholders and government agencies throughout project development, permitting, construction
and operations.

The plan includes a range of communication and engagement tools, including stakeholder
meetings, briefings, listening sessions, community events, Community Advisory Panel meetings,
online project facts, and other outreach materials that provide updates on project milestones,
construction activities, anticipated impacts, workforce opportunities and the broader benefits of
Commonwealth LNG and its presence in Cameron Parish. Two-way stakeholder engagement is
documented, evaluated as appropriate and considered in project planning and outreach efforts.

CWLNG Expansion Co has developed a project website which will provide publicly accessible
project      information,  updates,    and      relevant     resources.      The      website,
http://commonwealthexpansionproject.com, is expected to be available within the next few days.
CWLNG Expansion Co has designated a single point of contact to facilitate communications for
Project-related inquiries:
                                         Montana Patin
                              Director, Regulatory and Permitting
                                        (713) 600-6000
                                 montana.patin@caturus.com

Through its stakeholder engagement program, CWLNG Expansion Co seeks to strengthen
relationships with Cameron Parish residents, Police Jurors, elected officials, community
organizations, first responders, business leaders, commercial fishing stakeholders, and other key
community representatives. The program also supports community investment initiatives focused
on workforce development, education, public safety, coastal stewardship, economic development
and other local priorities.
 10.    Submittal to U.S. Coast Guard of Letter of Intent and Preliminary Waterways
       Suitability Assessment (18 C.F.R. § 157.21(d)(12))

CWLNG Expansion Co certifies that a Letter of Intent and updated WSA were submitted to the
USCG on September 15, 2026 (see Appendix E).

CWLNG Expansion Co respectfully requests that the Commission initiate the NEPA pre-filing
process by October 1, 2026. Should you have any questions about this request, please feel free to
contact the undersigned.


Respectfully submitted,

/s/JD Morris

JD Morris
VP, Regulatory & Permitting
jd.morris@caturus.com
